R_market_reversal.state: previous20days cumulative return of daily equalweighted available150 proxy,negative triggers; proxy excludes flagged corporate-action returns
R_market_reversal.beta: previous60 adjusted returns beta to same daily proxy; require>=40paired finite days; unknown multiplier1
R_market_reversal.allocation: base mild weight divided by (1+max(beta,0)) in negative state; otherwise base mild; normalize total90pct with existing1.8-5.4pct bounds
R_market_reversal.meaning: lower estimated sensitivity inside same25, not remove overall market exposure

E_overextension.definition: previous20days cumulative adjusted return minus mean of those20 path levels, divided by populationstd of20pathlevels; equivalent latest price relative20day mean in action-adjusted units
E_overextension.trigger: last adjusted level >mean+2std, multiplier .75; else1; unknown1
E_overextension.allocation: mild raw weight times multiplier, normalize90pct using same1.8-5.4pct bounds
E_overextension.meaning: a simple fixed extension rule, not claim all big winners reverse

S_common_risk.industry_data: no verified point-in-time individual classifications in retained sources; industry cap backtest not feasible
S_common_risk.diagnostic: prior60day mean pairwise correlation of selected25 adjusted returns; pair requires>=40finite days; groups <.25,.25-.5,>=.5 fixed
S_common_risk.not_industry: correlation is statistical common risk, not a reconstructed industry classification

T_turnover.candidate: reuse existing A_mild_tolerance; no new allocation parameter or cycle search
T_turnover.attribution: record exact replay settlement costs by initial entry,new later entry,full exit,retained adjust; reconcile return/fees to saved v7
T_turnover.causality: fee difference alone not counterfactual PnL; replay only to obtain trade attribution, not a duplicate candidate
